title: ISRO: From Aryabhata to Chandrayaan and Aditya

cards.b: India began with a rocket carried on a bicycle and now lands on the Moon. ISRO is known for low-cost, application-first space work: satellites for communication, weather and farming, then planetary science.

Vikram Sarabhai started INCOSPAR in 1962; ISRO was formed on 15 August 1969, and the Department of Space in 1972. First satellite Aryabhata (19 April 1975), then Bhaskara (1979), and SLV-3 (1980) put Rohini in orbit, making India the sixth country with orbital launch ability.

The INSAT series (from 1982) gave communications, television and weather forecasting. The IRS series (from 1988) images land and water for farming, forests and disasters. NavIC is India's regional navigation system, and EDUSAT served education. The PSLV (operational 1994) launched 104 satellites in one mission on 15 February 2017.

Chandrayaan-1 (22 October 2008) found water molecules on the Moon. Chandrayaan-2 (July 2019) orbiter works, but its Vikram lander crashed on 7 September 2019. Chandrayaan-3 launched on 14 July 2023 and landed near the lunar south pole on 23 August 2023, making India the fourth country to soft-land on the Moon and the first near the south pole. 23 August is celebrated as National Space Day. Chandrayaan-4 (a sample return mission) was approved in 2024.

cards.h: Mars, Sun and eyes on the cosmos
cards.b: Mangalyaan reached Mars orbit on 24 September 2014 on its first try. AstroSat (28 September 2015) is India's multi-wavelength space observatory. Aditya-L1 launched 2 September 2023, reached its L1 halo orbit on 6 January 2024. XPoSat (1 January 2024) studies X-ray polarisation from black holes and neutron stars.

SpaDeX (launched December 2024) achieved India's first in-orbit docking in January 2025, making India the fourth country to do so. NISAR, a NASA-ISRO radar satellite, launched in 2025 to map Earth's surface changes. Gaganyaan aims to send three Indian astronauts to about 400 km for three days, with uncrewed test flights first. As of late 2026 no crewed flight had flown; the first is targeted for 2027. Group Captain Shubhanshu Shukla flew to the ISS on Axiom-4 in 2025. A Bharatiya Antariksh Station is planned, with a Venus orbiter mission and an Indian on the Moon by 2040 as goals.

ISRO's record includes failures: PSLV's first flight (1993) failed, and Chandrayaan-2's lander crashed. Each analysis fed back: Chandrayaan-3 used a redesigned lander with a larger landing zone, and succeeded. The Pragyan rover measured surface temperature, found sulphur, and the lander detected moonquakes.

• 'Low cost means low quality.' Frugality comes from reuse of design, a skilled workforce and lower labour cost.
  • 'Chandrayaan-3 landed at the pole.' It landed about 69 degrees south, near it, the nearest any soft landing had come.
  • 'ISRO only builds rockets.' Most work is applications for daily life.

In 2020 the government opened the sector with IN-SPACe to authorise private players, and NSIL commercialises ISRO technology. Skyroot's Vikram-S (November 2022) was India's first privately built rocket to fly, and Agnikul launched from its own private pad in 2024.

• ISRO began 1962 to 1969 and launched Aryabhata in 1975.
  • Services: INSAT, IRS, NavIC; workhorse PSLV; heavy lifter LVM3.
  • Missions: Chandrayaan-3 (2023, south pole), Mangalyaan (2014), Aditya-L1 (2023), AstroSat (2015).
  • Next: Gaganyaan, docking, a space station, private industry.

Think about it: (1) Why does a south-pole landing matter? (2) How can private firms help ISRO?
